same_sign_failure.seam_real_part: if theta(q_+)=u+i v then Re D_same=diag(u,-u)
same_sign_failure.consequence: unless u=0, the reactive law mixes coherent and dark parity sectors

opposite_green_sign.interpretation: the minus is the opposite Green orientation of the reciprocal sheet, not a fitted phase

uniqueness.condition: the seam Hermitian/reactive real part commutes with exchange for generic q_+
uniqueness.result: epsilon_-=-epsilon_+; the relative sign is forced, up to one overall Green sign

scope.proved: the strict prime-delay Cayley complement can respect dark-channel parity only with opposite reciprocal Green signs
scope.not_proved: that this raw Cayley complement is the complete arithmetic diagonal or has the required p^-2 endpoint normalization
scope.retained_warning: prior asymptotic work rejects the raw Cayley law as the full diagonal reciprocal response coefficient; it remains admissible as a zero-free passive complement

next_assembly_test: Apply the same exchange-plus-Green-sign audit to endpoint, square, connected, and archimedean reactive terms. Every complete seam term must have equal parity-diagonal real parts, or paired anti-oriented contributions whose total does.
conclusion: Reciprocal parity already fixes the arithmetic complement's sheet sign. Using the same Cayley sign on both sheets breaks the protected dark channel; opposite Green orientation makes its seam reactive part scalar and parity preserving.
